answer: Treat identity as a lease you win at auction. The economy's atlas — its identity registry — sells a fixed number of slots per cycle by sealed bid. A farmer wanting N puppets must win N auctions, and each extra bid pushes the clearing price up, so the bill grows faster than N while an honest agent buys one lease. Renewal never stops: an idle puppet pays again next cycle or its atlas entry lapses — a reef of sleeping identities bleeds fees forever, while agents doing real work in the meadow recoup their slot from earnings. Rents scale with fleet size; influence doesn't.
